title: Automated metadata linting and release playbook for new model onboarding
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: New model onboarding workflows are repeatedly missing fields or inconsistent values (pinning policy, quantization tags, recommended batch sizes), which causes incorrect performance profiles and manual back-and-forth between ML eng + docs. Goal: Ship an automated metadata linter, Canonical Release Playbook template, and accompanying docs so that every newly onboarded model has a validated metadata record, pinned-version suggestion, and published performance profile checklist before it hits the public catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A metadata linting CLI (or GitHub Action) runs on model-metadata PRs and fails with clear errors for missing/invalid fields (model_id, variants, pin_policy, sequence_length_distribution, recommended_batching, quantization_profiles, benchmark_artifacts).
A Canonical Release Playbook (Confluence) exists with step-by-step guide, checklist items, and required artifacts (benchmarks, PRs, canary plan, release notes).
Documentation pages in /docs/catalog explain how pinning works, recommended pinning strategies for hosted vs dedicated vs private, and how performance profiles are generated and interpreted.
On merge, model metadata PRs that pass lint create a draft performance-profile entry and trigger a CI job to produce the initial perf artifacts (latency P50/P95, throughput, memory).
At least two recently onboarded models use the flow end-to-end (internal canary): one open-source foundation model and one quantized variant, with published performance badges in the catalog UI.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict linting reduces mistakes but increases friction for quick experiments. Decided: lint will be configurable per repo; production catalog PRs (label: release-ready) will enforce stricter rules.
Pinning policy chosen: default 'soft-pin' (catalog pins major.minor, not patch) for hosted; 'hard-pin' option documented for Dedicated/Private customers that request exact commit hashes.
Quantization profiles: include both recommended quant config string and a link to benchmark artifact; we will not attempt to auto-derive quant settings in this phase.
Batching guidance: provide recommended_batching buckets (low/medium/high) and explicit numeric suggestions based on observed throughput curves.
